description: Relation profile architecture@1: the controlled identifiers admitted for Project Anatomy relation_claim.relation_type and requirement constraint.relation_type. A declared relation type is governable, not true, admitted, Evidence or approved. Time, phase, variant and building state are dimensions of the claim (validity, qualifier.ouvrage_state), never encoded in relation names.

excludes: Source-intake container relations owned by implementation source intake
Epistemic relations (contradicts, derived_from, depends_on a decision), carried by Observation Bundles, derivation_refs, WorkIssues and Decision Requests

families.description: Source-to-project alignment and identity lifecycle (replacement, split, merge, supersession).
Topological relations between spaces, zones and the elements located in them.
Architectural relations between elements and spaces: hosting, openings, separation, passage.
Composition of an object from parts or layers.
Typing of an occurrence by a type definition.
Project grouping of objects (zones, sets, groups).
Constructive junctions between elements, including deliberate absence of connection.
Physical load paths between elements. Not the structural analysis model.
Relations between the project and its surroundings: neighbouring buildings, plots, public domain.

qualifier_vocabularies.description: Physical state of the building to which the relation applies. Replacing a claim is only meaningful between claims on the same state; projected versus executed is compared, never superseded.
Kind of containment, aligned with IFC: decomposition of spatial structure, primary containment of an element (at most one), or additional reference to further spatial structures.
Junction typology between two elements. corner, tee and cross have indicative IFC path-connection readings; butt and mitre have no IFC enumeration value.
Whether a source representation covers the whole stable object or only part of it.
Basis of a party-wall statement: legal presumption, established by title, or unknown.

entries.definition: The source representation (subject) is an occurrence of the stable project object (object).

ifc.note: The GlobalId stays a source-native identifier on the source representation; it never becomes Pantheon identity.

entries.notes: Several models (architecture, structure, MEP, survey, as-built) yield several representations of one object. A re-export with new GlobalIds yields new representations and new candidate matches, never a new object.

entries.definition: The stable object (subject) is retired and replaced by another stable object (object).
The stable object (subject) is split; the object is one of the resulting stable objects.
The stable object (subject) is merged into the resulting stable object (object).
The stable object (subject) supersedes an earlier stable object identity (object) while both remain addressable.
The spatial object (subject) contains the object (object): a sub-space by decomposition, an element by primary containment, or an element by additional reference.

ifc.note: containment=decomposition: site, building, storey and space decomposition.
containment=primary: an element is contained in at most one spatial structure.
containment=referenced: additional structures for elements spanning several storeys.

entries.definition: The object (subject) is located in the spatial object (object). Reading inverse of spatial.contains.
entries.notes: At most one primary location per element; referenced locations may be several.

entries.definition: Two spatial objects share a boundary.

ifc.note: No direct IFC space-to-space adjacency; derive from corresponding second-level boundaries or a shared bounding element.

entries.definition: The opening element (subject), such as a door, window or opening, gives onto the spatial object (object).

ifc.note: Derive from the boundaries of the door or opening toward each space.

entries.definition: The element (subject) is hosted by the host element (object), for example a door by a wall.

ifc.note: IFC never relates the door to the wall directly: wall, opening, door.

bot.note: Reading from the host; bot:hostsElement is deprecated in BOT.

entries.definition: The object (subject) is a part or layer of the composed object (object).

ifc.note: Element decomposition into parts; material layers are carried by material associations, not relations.

entries.definition: The occurrence (subject) is typed by the type definition (object).
The object (subject) belongs to the project group or zone (object).

ifc.note: Includes IfcZone groupings of spaces.

entries.definition: The spatial object (subject) is bounded by the element (object).

ifc.note: RelatingSpace to RelatedBuildingElement. Subtypes IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel and 2ndLevel; physical or virtual and internal or external are attributes, not subtypes.

entries.definition: The object (subject) is vertically above the object (object).

ifc.note: No IFC relation; derive from storey elevation, slab boundaries or geometry. IfcRelAggregates implies no order.

entries.definition: The object (subject) is vertically below the object (object). Reading inverse of spatial.above.
The element (subject) separates the spatial object (object) from another one; one claim per separated space.

ifc.note: The element is the related element of a boundary of each space. Open-plan separations use IfcVirtualElement.

entries.notes: Basis for inherited requirements: a separating element inherits the requirements of the pair of spaces it separates.

entries.definition: The spatial object (subject) is connected for passage through the element (object), such as a door or opening; one claim per connected space.

ifc.note: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement is MEP-only and does not apply.

entries.notes: Chains of connects_via and opens_to support derived circulation and accessibility paths.

entries.definition: The opening or void (subject) cuts through the host element (object).

ifc.note: RelatingBuildingElement is the host; RelatedOpeningElement is the opening. Read in reverse.

entries.notes: Covers reservations (trémies, fourreaux, réservations) as elements.

entries.definition: The element (subject), such as a door or window, fills the opening (object).

ifc.note: RelatingOpeningElement is the opening; RelatedBuildingElement is the filling element. Read in reverse.

entries.definition: Two elements are constructively joined.

ifc.note: Walls and other path elements. Indicative, non-normative reading: corner = ATSTART/ATEND on both, tee = ATPATH/ATEND, cross = ATPATH/ATPATH. butt and mitre have no enumeration value.
Generic connection without typology.

entries.notes: The junction is where most interfaces between work packages and most pathologies occur.

entries.definition: Two elements are deliberately kept unconnected, such as an acoustic decoupling or an expansion joint.

ifc.note: IFC has no relation for a deliberate absence of connection.

entries.notes: A positive named relation, because absence of a claim is not a negative claim.

entries.definition: The element (subject) transfers load onto the element (object).

ifc.note: No direction convention in IFC.
Support through a realizing element such as a bearing.

entries.notes: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember belongs to the structural analysis model and is deliberately not mapped. Structural statements require validation by a structural engineer.

entries.definition: The element (subject) carries the load of the element (object). Reading inverse of structure.bears_on.
The separating element (subject) is shared with, or bounds, a neighbouring building or plot (object).

ifc.note: Covers a neighbouring building only; a party wall with an unbuilt plot and legal co-ownership have no IFC representation.

entries.notes: The legal status is a qualifier: presumed, established by title or unknown. Neighbouring objects carry no third-party personal data.
